newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares close up but could halt on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares close up but could halt on Wednesday.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Tuesday, with the firm dollar a major factor fuelling advances in top shares and high turnover, but dealers saw prices levelling out on Wednesday.

"There has been an unusually amount of liquidity in the market and turnover has been high. The strong dollar has helped prices up too but I don't think we shall see more rises now and prices should keep to present levels tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 2.18 point to close at 155.88 while the KFX March future rose 2.75 point to 156.00 with 780 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Novo Nordisk rose 25 crowns to end the day at 657, driven by the strong dollar and the company's hopes of helping to develop a vaccine against diabetes.
Like telecoms sector shares elsewhere Tele Danmark made gains. It closed 13 up, at 357 crowns, in turnover of 476,000 shares traded.
Both companies' shares continued to edge up in early Wall Street trade after the Copenhagen close.
Overall turnover for the day on the Danish exchange was 1.29 billion crowns.
